## Result

- Skill: design-review
- Review status: changes-requested
- Package members: Skill and the scoped System amendment, plus the exact retained source clauses, pilot resources and producer/consumer interactions identified below and in subjects.
- Upstream review ID: proposal-review (approved; exact proposal identity unchanged).
- Review ID and round: design-review-r1, round 1.
- Material findings: skl-dr-001.
- Correction targets: skill, owning stage design.
- Recording status: recorded on successful primary batch persistence.
- Open blockers: no missing authority or evidence; one required design correction remains.
- Immediate next stage: isolated stop; return the finding to the author through route under existing authority.
- Claim limitations: no Design approval, plan reliance, implementation, pilot conformance, adoption, final Verify, publication or customer-installation authorization.

## Independence and assessment basis

The parent design author created Skill, amended System and authored the retained-contract correction; the user supplied direction and correction requirements. Independent agent /root/independent_design_review authored none of those contributions and made no engineering edits. This reviewer inspected the exact final models and their retained-source/consumer basis and owns this judgment and finding.

This is formal-lifecycle/manual review, isolated downstream. Complete Skill and System models, complete Skill Contract, Readability and Customer Portability sources, the resource-integrity ADR, approved proposal and prior Proposal Review were assessed. The prior authoring evidence is an earlier-subject snapshot; the retained-contract correction and current registered subjects identify the corrected basis. No prior author self-assessment is treated as independent approval.

The selected legacy member scopes are Skill Contract's mapped common clauses and complete disposition context, Readability's and Portability's common rules and historical rollout distinctions, the whole resource-integrity ADR, and the mixed architecture's resource flow items 1-10, Crosscutting resource-integrity section, validation building-block boundary and corresponding decision entry. Retained plan/method duties and all other architecture sections are excluded from transfer. Proposal simplification's common-body/conditional-reference/output ownership, Proposal Review simplification's classification/recording/gate/result rules, proposal-family PFA-R1-32 and published-skill-first R24-29 supply scoped compatibility and proof evidence. Their older storage procedures are subordinate to Constitution and the adopted v2-only profile; no retired runtime is reinstated.

Inspected both complete canonical pilot bodies, every existing pilot asset and conditional reference, and their unchanged shared assessment/requirement guidance. Inspected actual targeted-profile validation, installed-review placement detection, and supported archive profile comparison. The early-return and heading-dependent consumer hazards stated by the author are real. No independent extra skill is pulled into the improvement scope. The no-map rationale is appropriate: the historical project inventory was not used as a current dependency audit.

## Eight-criterion package assessment

| Criterion | Assessment | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Realization supports behavior and failures | pass with required correction below | Classification before recording, complete existing conditional references, explicit late triggers and body stops can realize the named pilot outcomes. No new service or schema is necessary. The retained lint outcomes need the correction in criterion 8 before implementation allocation can rely on them. |
| 2. Real constraints and compatibility | concern | V2-only recording, portable authority, unchanged specialist policies and no customer activation are respected. Existing non-pilot lint applicability is referenced but insufficiently defined at its proposed replacement owner (skl-dr-001). |
| 3. Feasibility does not weaken approved goals | pass | A useful navigation/procedure correction is grounded in inspected baseline; old asset extraction and invocation descriptions are recognized as strengths. No savings quota, model-only substitute or additional pilot is selected. |
| 4. System, authority, recovery and external boundaries | pass | System's prospective owner transfer is conditional on reviewed implementation and Verify. Recording, assessment, Test, distribution, installation and release stay separately owned. Failed/missing resources and stale or interrupted writes have explicit scoped stops. |
| 5. Decision preservation | pass | SKL-DEC-01-05 preserve material rationale and alternatives, including raw-byte parity, false-positive lint avoidance and package/fallback separation; original ADR identities and judgments stay readable. No unsupported target-runtime gate is revived. |
| 6. One common owner and reconciled consumers | concern | Selected owner and pilot profile/placement/archive consumers are coherent. The retained lint contract still needs precise definitions at that owner before the selected source definitions become historical (skl-dr-001). |
| 7. Credible bases and representative outcomes | pass | Eight dimensions and four concrete combined hazards supply local/integrated observation boundaries for Delivery. Ordinary versus governed/durable paths, missing versus untriggered resources, raw bytes and non-pilot coexistence are distinguishable. Mechanical checks do not substitute for usefulness assessment. |
| 8. Complete bounded migration | changes required | Metadata, role fields/summary, vocabulary presentation, output equivalence and asset scope now have precise definitions with supported amendments. But common public-lint scope and legacy resource failure/enforcement conditions remain abbreviated preservation references while their defining sources are selected for retirement; see skl-dr-001. Archive byte/link safeguards and 17-skill follow-up families otherwise retain the approved boundary. |

## Finding skl-dr-001

- Finding ID: skl-dr-001
- Severity: medium; required before package approval because it controls source retirement and validator compatibility.
- Location: docs/design/skill/skill.md:60 and source-qualified displacement rows at lines 160, 173 and 175; retained-contract table begins at line 130.
- Evidence: Skill lines 160, 173 and 175 declare transfer of Skill Contract R3i/j and R49-R53 into SKL-SR-02/05/08-10/14/15, while SKL-SR-14 (line 60) and the retained-contract table only supply general bounded checks and preservation language. The common owner does not define R3i/j's scope: checks cover canonical shipped text, generated public copies and adapter copies, and exclude internal specs, plans, tests, generator scripts and maintainer/contributor docs. Nor does it state R49b/d's precise recognized-loading-instruction/prefix boundary (including legacy templates/) and fail-or-explicitly-approved-temporary-exception outcome. The R53 row says to retain existing audit/debt applicability and no new debt, but does not state R53a's immediate full enforcement for new/changed skills versus R53b's clean-audit-or-review-visible-disposition condition for inventory-wide enforcement, or identify an adopted supersession of those populations. The same definition is selected for replacement in mixed architecture Runtime View resource-integrity items 1-7 and Crosscutting resource integrity. A maintainer cannot decide the preserved lint population and permitted exception from the new owner alone; retired prose would still supply the decision.
- Required outcome: Define the surviving public-text lint scope and resource migration/enforcement rules directly in Skill, with their applicable populations and exact approved supersessions or temporary-exception conditions. A maintainer must be able to determine whether an internal contributor document is exempt and whether an unmapped legacy instruction in a new/changed versus unchanged skill fails or has a valid temporary disposition without rebuilding the rule from archived prose. Keep historical initial audit execution historical; do not reset enforcement or invent a new global audit. If an obligation is already superseded, name that disposition and its approving owner; otherwise transfer its precise condition and outcome or explicitly retain the source clause as current until resolved.
- Safe resolution path: The design author adds compact retained-contract rows or equivalent precise normative prose for the cited safeguards, reconciles the source mappings and author evidence, and returns the changed package for independent reassessment. Do not edit skills, execute adoption, retire sources, or broaden the pilot to repair this design finding. No new owner decision is required to preserve existing rules.
- needs-decision rationale: none; preservation is already required by the approved direction, the user's correction and Design DES-SR-13.
- Finding scope: artifact-local.
- Affected artifact IDs: skill.
- Owning stages: design.

This is one bounded preservation finding, not a demand to copy every historical source clause. It does not dispute the corrected metadata/role/vocabulary rows or require re-running completed pilot experiments.

## Evidence and recording limits

Commands actually used: read-only cat/sed/rg inspections; repository-local primary context with full selected activity/model/proposal/review/finding/blocker/applicability fields; subject inspect --content full --max-bytes 8388608 for 34 exact subjects; review record --help and finding add --help; primary batch recording of this review and its finding. Subject inspection supplied raw-byte identities and the batch checks exact reads and current revision. No engineering tests or package generation were run by this reviewer: this is semantic Design assessment, not implementation proof. Author-reported structural/prose checks were inspected for their stated scope and do not settle semantic preservation.

Approval is withheld until the author supplies the precise remaining retained contract and this package is independently reassessed. Historical source definitions remain current under the existing adoption boundary in the meantime.
